content.intro: Learn migration operations through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Migration Operations matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines migration operations as part of database configuration, migrations, and transactions. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Creating and deleting models; Adding, renaming, and altering fields; Changing model relationships; Schema and data changes; Understanding migration dependencies. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Creating and deleting models
items.text: Creating and deleting models affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Creating and deleting models. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
